# External records (append-only)

Downloaded 19 Nov 2026 from official publishers only (Vahid approved: the November 2026 MPR comparator, the data to score the 2026Q3 forecasts, and source-level seasonally adjusted euro-area and German CPI). Each raw file was saved to its own new directory outside the repo and read as untrusted data with `python -I`. Only the values used are committed here; the raw files are not, and `data/boe_var_data.csv` is not changed. Append new files or rows; do not edit these.

Notes
- The ECB's older adjusted key `ICP.M.U2.Y.000000.3.INX` stops at 2025-12 (superseded by the 2025 = 100 `HICP` dataset); it was downloaded and not used.
- **German CPI seasonally adjusted at source: not obtained.** Destatis serves its tables through GENESIS, whose download service needs an account login; it was not used. The ECB portal has no adjusted HICP for Germany (`HICP.M.DE.Y.000000.4F0.INX` returns 404). The German series only backcasts the euro-area leg before 1997, so the check in `results/ecb_seasonal_check.md` starts in 1997Q2.
- MGSC and MGRZ hashes: MGSC `2d1417ac9a45cea5ef622ded4c16656e2c730579c1227e212b30b7d8cd53349d`, MGRZ `c194fecaebac15c9501520447738b923b7290e8dac83c79364ee770bd5275033`.
- Used by `scripts/score_2026q3.py` (→ `results/score_2026q3.md`), `scripts/compare_ecb_seasonal.py` (→ `results/ecb_seasonal_check.md`) and the November MPR section of `results/forecast_vs_boe_obr.md`.
- **`brignone_piffer_2025_fig2_fig3_irf_medians.csv` is a reading of a figure, not a published table (25 Nov 2026).** The paper gives its impulse responses only as Figures 2 and 3, and there is no replication package. In the PDF those figures are vector drawings: each panel's median is a stroked line with one vertex per quarter, and each panel has a line at zero. `scripts/extract_paper_irf_medians.py` reads the vertices from the file. The one thing it cannot read is the text of the y-axis tick labels (stored as glyph outlines), so those are transcribed by hand in the script, from a 250 dpi rendering, and checked against the drawing: the number of labels, the number of digits in each, even spacing in the transcribed values, and the implied zero against the drawn zero line. All 48 panels pass. Independent checks in `tests/test_irf_benchmark.py`: the medians are zero on impact exactly where Table 2 imposes a zero (10 responses), have the Table 2 sign on impact everywhere it imposes one (23 responses), and agree with the paper's prose in section 3.1. Limits: coordinates sit on a 0.12 pt grid, so each value is good to about half a grid step (`resolution` column; 0.8% of the panel's largest response for the median panel, under 6% for all); six medians in Figure 3 had one vertex dropped by the PDF writer because it lay on the straight line between its neighbours, and it is restored by linear interpolation; a consistent misreading of every label of one panel that kept digit counts and spacing would not be caught (`tick_step` records what each value rests on). The authors have not confirmed these numbers. Only the medians are read; the 68% and 90% sets are filled shapes clipped to the axes and were not extracted. PyMuPDF (AGPL) is needed to re-run the script and is not a project dependency: `uv run --with pymupdf python scripts/extract_paper_irf_medians.py`.
- Used by `scripts/run_irf_reference.py` (→ `results/irf_reference.json`, `results/irf_vs_paper.md`).
